adaptations: Each original parameter expansion is a separately reported Rust #[test] with its exact frozen source ID. The native assertions execute actual storage, archive, crypto, HTTP, CLI-domain, process and installation APIs against owned temporary roots.

Python monkeypatches at filesystem operations correspond to explicit test-support callbacks at actual native reads, physical resolution, atomic create_new/replace, rollback, session rename/reclaim, copy, conversion and selection boundaries. Product builds exclude observer state and hook calls. Callbacks may fail, park, or reproduce the original no-op filesystem operation only under this feature.

Cross-process cases re-execute the exact Rust test under ownership::capture. Workers synchronize through bounded owned file rendezvous and execute real independent native repositories and OS locks; no Python interpreter, Python oracle, shell process stand-in, or extra helper test is used.

Scheduler activation runs the actual Runtime/Adapter/Registry and a compiled native SDK fixture; the fixture starts a real browser leaf inside the owned process tree. Startup, exit and shutdown assertions observe actual child lifetimes and durable schedule outcomes.

The source Python fallback-identity test inspected SHA256(ctimestr) implementation and stability across three interpreters. Native ownership uses stable kernel creation tokens and refuses unavailable birth identities. Its mapped case observes the same real PID token from three native children and asserts fail-closed unavailability; no fallback hash or fake PID is introduced.

Explicit path/environment discovery arguments replace global HOME/USERPROFILE/sys.frozen monkeypatches. An owned ordinary file occupying the required directory path provides a portable unwritable-directory failure even when the test process is privileged.

HTTP source fault cases that let OSError escape TestClient become actual native HTTP 500 responses, followed by the same exact rollback/no-write filesystem assertions. Response text is retained where native error responses are not JSON.

Pure network destination checks pass the original URL and a deterministic DNS observation through the actual parse/public-address/pinning function. Rebinding asserts that the validated address remains fixed and a later loopback resolution is refused. Private actual rotate requests exercise native refusal before connection.

Python numeric equality accepts integral float/int representations; native JSON assertions compare corresponding numeric values where the public model normalizes to float. Nonfinite in-memory values are inserted directly without serializing through JSON.

Installation tests use real shared/exclusive file locks and an owned copy of the actual native engine, checking activation refusal before a deliberately invalid CLI argument could be parsed. No process-global installation or user data is probed.
Original cryptography/FastAPI optional dependencies are native target dependencies, so none of the mapped tests is skipped.
